dno_dashboard.intro: Korea's distribution sector is a SINGLE-DSO MONOPOLY (cohort-UNIQUE first). KEPCO — Korea Electric Power Corporation (한국전력공사) — owns and operates all transmission + distribution + retail sales infrastructure across the entire Korean Peninsula (excluding DPRK). KEPCO is majority government-owned (Korea Development Bank + Korean state). HQ in Naju-si, Jeollanam-do. The TSO function is split: KPX (Korea Power Exchange) is the market + system operator (non-profit under MOTIE); KEPCO holds the physical transmission assets. This MO-TO split is also cohort-UNIQUE. The 6 generation subsidiaries (KOSEPCO + KOSPO + KOMIPO + KOWEPO + KEWESPO + KHNP) were spun out in 2001 restructuring but remain under KEPCO holding. 24 nuclear reactors operational (KHNP-operated, ~32% generation share — cohort-highest).

b2_voll_note: Value of Lost Load (VoLL) context — Korea-localized: Korean industrial VoLL is estimated at ₩25,000–45,000/kWh (≈ €18–32/kWh) for chaebol fab + petrochemical corridors (Samsung Pyeongtaek, SK Hynix Icheon, POSCO Gwangyang/Pohang, Hyundai Ulsan) — among the highest single-site VoLL exposures in OECD coverage due to chaebol concentration. Residential VoLL is ~₩1,400–5,500/kWh (≈ €1–4/kWh). The SSI's R3 consequence multiplier identifies which substations serve the most economically exposed territories. {totalHCHR} substations combine Industrial-Chaebol economic fabric (R3 ≥ {topLower}) with High or Critical risk classification — representing the highest VoLL-weighted exposure in the Korean fleet.
b2_narrative: The Industrial-Chaebol tier concentrates in {econRegionStr} — Korean do/si where chaebol fab + steel + petrochemical corridors depend on uninterrupted 765/345/154 kV transmission for continuous semiconductor lithography, blast furnaces, and ethylene crackers. A single hour of unplanned outage at these substations carries an estimated VoLL of ₩25,000–45,000/kWh (≈ €18–32/kWh) for fab corridors, compared to ₩1,400–5,500/kWh (≈ €1–4/kWh) in rural agricultural Gangwon + Jeju. The fleet-wide average energy poverty rate is {avgEP}%, but this masks sharp regional variation: peripheral do/si (Gangwon highlands, Jeju isolated HVDC sub-grid) combine higher energy poverty with higher R6_typhoon exposure, creating a double vulnerability that the E component captures. This cross-referencing of chaebol-driven economic fabric with KEPCO single-DSO monopoly grid condition is unique to Korea — Samsung Pyeongtaek alone consumes more electricity than several entire do/si.
